sides.name: British Eighth Army
sides.note: Strength (Wikipedia infobox): 195,000 men, 1,029 tanks (high ~1,350 incl. tanks in workshops and reserve), 435 armoured cars (entered as ifv_apc), 892-908 field and medium guns, 1,451 anti-tank guns (not counted as artillery), 730-750 aircraft. infantry_line: seven infantry divisions (9th Aus, 2nd NZ, 51st, 50th, 44th, 4th Ind, 1st SA) plus motor battalions, ~35-45% of ration strength, educated split. Fighter/strike split of the Desert Air Force (Hurricane, Kittyhawk, Spitfire vs Boston, Baltimore, Wellington) is educated. Tech (derived:tech-anchor, 1942 just below 1943 anchor): logistics 7.9 = fully motorised with short LOC to Alexandria; ISR 7.9 = Ultra plus air reconnaissance. Ratings: command 0.7 (Montgomery's set-piece planning, trained staff); morale 0.7 (re-equipped, Alam Halfa success); training 0.65. Surprise: Operation Bertram deception concealed timing and main effort. riverCrossing false: the attack went through minefields in open desert, no river (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Battle_of_El_Alamein).

sides.name: German-Italian Panzer Army Africa
sides.note: Strength (Wikipedia infobox): 116,000 men (~50,000 German, ~66,000 Italian), 547 tanks (German ~249 incl. ~30 Pz IV Special, Italian ~280-298 M13/M14), 192 armoured cars, 552 guns, 496-1,063 anti-tank guns (not counted), 770-900 aircraft (many unserviceable). infantry_line ~40-50% of strength (164th, 90th Light, Ramcke, Folgore, Bologna, Brescia, Pavia, Trento), educated. Aircraft split educated. Tech: armor 7.5 (Italian M13/40 obsolete); logistics 6.8 (LOC >1,000 km to Tobruk/Benghazi, fuel shortages from Ultra-directed sinkings); fortification 7.8 = 'Devil's Gardens' minefields of c. 500,000 mines (Wikipedia) with outposts in depth. Ratings: command 0.6 (Stumme died 24 Oct, Rommel back 25 Oct, mixed German-Italian command); morale 0.5; training 0.6 (Afrika Korps veterans, weaker Italian infantry). prepared true: Rommel had time to fortify the line, sowing about 500,000 mines and miles of barbed wire (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Battle_of_El_Alamein, citing Bierman and Smith 2003 p.255).

outcome.note: 23 Oct - 4 Nov 1942 (Operations Lightfoot and Supercharge; Axis withdrawal ordered 4 Nov). Eighth Army 13,560 casualties (infobox), 332-500 tanks knocked out (many repaired). Axis 41,800-73,000 casualties incl. ~30,000 prisoners; ~500 tanks destroyed. Mid is the centre of the published range, not a measured value.
